_readme: Regression claims. `expected` is ground truth. `acceptable` is the set of verdicts the keyless (heuristic) pipeline may return - hard cases allow 'Unverified' (honest abstention), but a polarity inversion (True-side for a false claim or vice versa) is always a failure. Wikipedia evidence is a live snapshot recorded by scripts/record_fixtures.py; entries with `synthetic_evidence` are hand-written fact-checker items (NOT real articles) used to exercise the Misleading/Mixed paths.

claims.claim: The Eiffel Tower is located in Paris.
Albert Einstein won the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.
The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean on Earth.
Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun.
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
Humans only use 10% of their brains.
The Great Wall of China is visible from space with the naked eye.
Lightning never strikes the same place twice.
Napoleon Bonaparte was unusually short for his time.
Daily low-dose aspirin prevents heart attacks in healthy adults.
Crime in Springfield doubled last year.

synthetic_evidence.title: Springfield crime did not 'double' in any meaningful sense
synthetic_evidence.snippet: Springfield crime doubled last year from 2 to 4 reported incidents in one district; the claim is misleading because it omits the tiny absolute numbers and that citywide crime fell.

synthetic_evidence.title: Did crime double in Springfield?
synthetic_evidence.snippet: Springfield crime doubled in one district last year, but the claim lacks context: the absolute numbers were tiny and citywide totals declined.

claims.claim: Acme Corp cut its emissions by 40% since 2015.

synthetic_evidence.title: Acme Corp emissions claim
synthetic_evidence.snippet: Acme Corp says it cut its emissions by 40% since 2015. Reuters verified the figure against its audited filings.

synthetic_evidence.title: Acme Corp emissions claim
synthetic_evidence.snippet: Acme Corp claims it cut its emissions by 40% since 2015. Full Fact found the cut excludes supply-chain emissions and is false for total emissions.
